audit.whatIsWrong: The chart hands Gwen Levels 1, 2, 3 and 4-5, while the early text opens 'Levels 1-3 are genuinely Maokai's' and whys[3] says you have nothing to deny his saplings pre-mist.
audit.why: Gwen loses this lane at 48.87%. Sapling Toss plus Sap Magic wins the poke war until Hallowed Mist exists, and her only clear window is Riftmaker.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Maokai / Skill / Gwen / Skill in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is the pivot of the whole matchup and its cooldown is never stated.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s, Bramble Smash 7s at rank 1, Sapling Toss 18s and Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s. 'Force the duel when his W is down' means a 14-second window at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the spikes, whys, wants and cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says to let Twisted Advance land and THEN drop Hallowed Mist so he is 'stuck outside the fog and cannot target you'. Twisted Advance is a dash to the target — it puts him on top of you, inside the mist.
audit.why: Riot's text: Maokai 'contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target.' The correct play is the opposite order: stand in the mist BEFORE he casts. He cannot target you from outside it, so the root cannot be cast at all. Also worth knowing — he is untargetable for the whole dash, so damage you throw at the cast is wasted.
audit.corrected: Mist ordering inverted in wants.you[0], the level-6 spike and mid; the untargetable dash stated in Key Ability Interactions.

edits.before: Snip Snip! plus your E reset lets you contest, but his Twisted Advance root and sapling chip keep the lane genuinely even.
edits.after: Snip Snip! and your E reset let you contest, but Twisted Advance (W, 14s) and sapling chip keep the lane genuinely even.

edits.before: He scales as a tanky root-bot who never falls off, so even fully online you out-value rather than out-stat him.
edits.after: He scales as a tanky root-bot who never falls off, so even fully online you out-value him rather than out-stat him.

edits.before: Bait Twisted Advance into your Hallowed Mist so the root lands but his Bramble Smash and sapling pop whiff while he's stuck outside the fog and can't target you
edits.after: Stand INSIDE Hallowed Mist before he casts — Twisted Advance is a targeted dash, so from outside the fog he cannot pick you at all and the 14s root is wasted

edits.before: With Hallowed Mist down and Needlework up you can bait his Twisted Advance, drop W as the root lands so his Bramble Smash knockback whiffs, and out-sustain the brawl — this is where the lane equalizes.
edits.after: With Hallowed Mist and Needlework up, sit in the fog before he commits: Twisted Advance needs a target, so from outside he cannot cast the 14-second root at all — this is where the lane equalizes.

edits.before: A landed Twisted Advance (W) chains into Bramble Smash knockback plus a sapling pop — that's his only real kill sequence all game, so dodge the root or sit in your mist when it's down.
edits.after: A landed Twisted Advance (W, 14s) chains into Bramble Smash knockback plus a sapling pop — that is his only real kill sequence all game, so be standing in your mist before he ever casts it.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 even it out as you come online. Once you have Hallowed Mist you can finally punish his Twisted Advance — let the root land, drop W as it connects so his Bramble Smash knockback and sapling pop hit nothing while he's stuck outside your fog and can't target you. At 6, Needlework ramps the longer the brawl goes and your ability healing chews through his big HP bar, so extended fights are fine. Just never get rooted outside the mist with E down — that one sequence still flips the trade hard to him.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 even out as you come online. Once you have Hallowed Mist, stand in it before he commits: Twisted Advance is a targeted dash, so from outside the fog he cannot pick you and the 14-second root never happens. Do not throw damage at the cast either — he is untargetable for the whole dash. At 6, Needlework ramps the longer the brawl goes and your healing chews his big HP bar, so extended fights are fine. Just never get rooted outside the mist with E down; that one sequence still flips the trade to him.

edits.before: Track Maokai's Twisted Advance (Root): His lock-on root. Mist or dodge it. When it is down — Snip him in your mist.
edits.after: Twisted Advance (W, 14s) is untargetable through the dash and needs a target — from outside your mist he cannot cast it.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Mist or dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance (W): 14/13/12/11/10s — untargetable through the dash, and uncastable while you are in the mist and he is not. - Bramble Smash: 7s at rank 1. - Sapling Toss: 18s. - Nature's Grasp: 130/110/90s.

notes: The kit file gives Bramble Smash a derived 'grounding' flag and a 'knockup' flag, but Riot's own description says it knocks back and slows — no grounding, no knock-up. Per the trust-the-description rule I wrote knockback only and did not claim it stops Skip 'n Slash. If it does ground, that would be the most important line on the page, so it is worth a human check.
